root_idea.summary: The root centers on joining one thing to another, especially by matching, overlaying, or fastening pieces together.
root_idea.development: The core sense appears in sewing or doubling a sole and in making coverings from joined leaves. Related extensions describe woven palm-leaf objects, things in which two colors are brought together, and mixtures in which one substance is combined with another; a separate lexical branch concerns a female giving birth in the ninth month.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form خَصَفَ rather than the imperfect QAC lemma.

senses.definition: To fasten or join leaves together as a covering.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ, the two subjects attach leaves to themselves to cover their private parts. The sense involves joining the leaves together and applying them leaf by leaf as a covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of joining or putting things together; sewing or patching a sole by placing one piece over another, and making an object double or faced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same joining metaphorically describes one set of tracks covering another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be followed, said of a body of troops followed by horsemen.
To lie.
To exceed someone in reviling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression portrays reviling as being added upon reviling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sole having another sole sewn onto it.
A mixture or pattern of two colors, especially black and white.
A sole or matching piece sewn onto a sole to make it double.
A puncture or stitch-hole in a skin.
An orifice of the body, including the anus or the vaginal opening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or anatomical extension of the sense of an opening made by puncturing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A receptacle for dates made from palm leaves, or a palm-leaf mat used for drying food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote the material object and its plural or collective uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A very thick kind of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is reported alongside the palm-leaf meanings and is connected with the resemblance of the cloth to woven palm leaves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female camel or woman who gives birth in the ninth month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: For a camel, the term is associated with giving birth in the ninth month; descriptions of the exact timing vary among the cited authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Two-colored or mixed in color, especially black and white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to ashes, a rope, or other things in which the two colors are united; it can also describe a troop having two colors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A body of troops followed by horsemen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported alternative use of the expression for a troop.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh milk poured onto curdled or thick milk.
To make hair mixed white and black, as hoariness does.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II use describing hair whose white and dark portions occur in roughly equal proportions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To weave a palm-leaf mat or other خَصْفَة.
A person who sews or patches soles by attaching additional pieces.
A person who covers the pudendum with the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or bodily application of the covering sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A liar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative explanation presents the liar as sewing one statement onto another and embellishing it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Two-colored, especially black and white; also having a contrasting white or dark area.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to mountains, male ostriches, two-colored ropes, and horses or sheep with white along the flanks or sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An awl or perforating instrument used in sewing soles and similar work.
Smooth, said of a ewe or she-goat.
Black and white or otherwise two-colored, said of a ewe or she-goat.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Quran-attested leaf-joining and covering use is represented; an uncertain bathing-context transcription is noted separately.
Figurative covering of one set of tracks by another is included in the joining/overlaying meaning.
Feminine-form identification without an independent definition.

cautions: The Quranic occurrences are dual imperfect forms يَخْصِفَانِ, while the public dictionary headword is normalized to the Form I perfect خَصَفَ.
Lane reports alternate Quranic readings in Forms II, IV, and VIII; the supplied QAC grouping is authoritative here and is therefore represented as Form I only.
The palm-leaf and thick-cloth senses of خَصَفَةٌ include a reported lexicographical disagreement about the precise object meant.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: In lane-unit:xSf:19283:g1:sub3, a bathing-context phrase meaning covering the pudendum with the hand is explicitly described as possibly mistranscribed and its exact derived form is uncertain; the stable Quranic leaf-covering usage is represented, while the uncertain form is not assigned as a separate public headword.
